name: Independent cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 5

book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: Traditional air of reflection before king’s brought in to die

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the short word before it is read the other way
something brought in is taken inside, so the monarch's letters go inside the verb

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
K is the chess abbreviation for king, with the S of the possessive
to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A traditional tune of quiet reflection, sung before a king is brought in to be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: To die for something is to long for it. The king goes inside after the first letter of that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk song is a traditional melody handed down among ordinary people, and an air is a tune.

clue.text: Some hat, we are told, but not effective!

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: some is a few, and tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A hat is described as ineffective, an exasperated comment on headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A tile was once a slang word for a hat, especially a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile achieves nothing and is useless, which is the same as being ineffective.

clue.text: American flight to Masters for first day of August

blocks.note: on the lam is American slang for fleeing
Masters of Arts are MAs, joined on with to

explanation.surface: An American runs off to sit a Masters degree, but only for the first day of August.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas was the old English harvest festival on 1 August, when loaves of the new wheat were blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas Day is the traditional name of the harvest feast held on the first of August in England.

clue.text: Lioness or woman? You can’t make it out!

definitions.text: Lioness or woman? You can’t make it out!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone unsure whether a figure is an animal or a person
setter's reading: the Egyptian statue with a lion's body and a woman's head, a byword for being inscrutable

explanation.walkthrough: The creature is both lion and woman at once, and its enigmatic face is proverbially impossible to read.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Sphinx combines a lion's body with a human head, and an inscrutable person is called sphinx-like.

clue.text: Refusal to stick to the point occasionally

blocks.note: a refusal is a no
a wand is a slender stick
the article taken as written, with to as a joiner
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes refuses to keep to the point of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then is an idiom for from time to time, meaning occasionally rather than regularly.

clue.text: Strict disciplinarian for male staff

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A strict manager is put in charge of the men on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is figuratively a stiff, rigid person who enforces rules severely, like a drill sergeant.

clue.text: Briskness in the manner of run in London, say

indicators.note: in places the letter for run inside the place named afterwards

blocks.note: à la is French for in the style of
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Someone moves briskly, like a jogger running through London.
explanation.walkthrough: À la is borrowed French, common in English for in the style of.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is brisk and cheerful readiness, so it is a synonym for quickness or briskness of action.

clue.text: Note company’s extremely successful revival

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Co is the abbreviation for company, the 's reading as is
very and extremely are synonyms

explanation.surface: A business memo reports that the company has staged a highly successful comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A recovery is a return to health or prosperity, a revival that has worked.

clue.text: In attacking speech help to reverse national division

indicators.note: to reverse is to go backwards, so the word for help is read from right to left

blocks.note: aid is help, then turned round
a tribe is a division of a people or nation

explanation.surface: A speaker launches an attack meant to roll back a division in the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful and angry denunciation delivered in words.

clue.text: Weapon of cat against a predator

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A cat's only weapon against a swooping bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used by Native Americans as a tool and in war.

clue.text: Dash about in continent pursuing fellow

indicators.note: in puts the short word for about inside the continent
pursuing means coming behind, so the continent part follows the letter for fellow

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
Asia is a continent
c, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone dashes around a continent chasing a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb but is short for dashboard; c for circa is the dating abbreviation meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the fascia is the dashboard of a car, the panel holding its dials and controls.

clue.text: I’m left working hard for scholarship

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
earning is getting money by working

explanation.surface: A student says they have been left toiling away to win a scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a learner's boast: I'm L, earning, which also says I'm learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship is knowledge acquired by study, which is exactly what learning means as a noun.

clue.text: He’ll drive right into port

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the port's name

blocks.note: Dover is the English Channel port
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A driver says he will steer straight into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a car; a drover drives cattle or sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover is a man who herds livestock along to market, so he is the one who drives them.

clue.text: Employment department’s free to take counsel

blocks.note: DE was the initials of the UK Department of Employment
to liberate is to set free

explanation.surface: The jobs ministry is free to seek advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Department of Employment was the British government ministry for jobs and labour, abbreviated DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to consider carefully and discuss before deciding, which is taking counsel together.

clue.text: Treatment for a batterer’s neglected child

indicators.note: treatment works material over and changes it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these words, the S included

explanation.surface: Social services decide how to deal with an abuser whose child has been neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Street arab is an old, now offensive term for a homeless urchin left to roam the streets.

clue.text: Motive and method for elevated route

blocks.note: a cause is a motive or reason
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A detective weighs motive and method, as if planning a crime along a raised road.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a road or path raised on an embankment across low or wet ground.

clue.text: Deposit from hot springs outside is left here

indicators.note: outside means the deposit's letters wrap round the short word that follows

blocks.note: sinter is the mineral crust left by hot springs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guide points to where minerals from hot springs have built up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinter is a geology word for the silica or chalky crust that forms round geysers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for left and survives in heraldry for the left side of a shield.

clue.text: To speculate in gold is admitted by you

indicators.note: what is admitted by something is let inside it, so these letters go within the pronoun

blocks.note: thee is the old form of you
or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone invites you to gamble on the gold market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speculate in gold' sounds like investing; here speculate means to form theories.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas and conjectures about something, which is what it means to speculate.

clue.text: Subject — smash hit, with time, in part of circle

indicators.note: to smash something is to break it to pieces, so these letters are scrambled
in places the scrambled letters inside the part of a circle

blocks.note: an arc is part of a circle's circumference
taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A record smashes into the charts, going round and round in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash hit' reads as a chart-topping record, but smash is the anagram signal for hit with time.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic, the study of numbers and calculation, is a school subject.

clue.text: Company support for office equipment

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A firm's backing is sought to buy new office kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier is a photocopying machine, a standard item in any workplace.

clue.text: Measure abnormal growth in progress

blocks.note: a gall is an abnormal swelling on a plant
something on is happening now

explanation.surface: Doctors measure a tumour while it is still growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of liquid volume, eight pints, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Emergency when crop’s half destroyed by river

indicators.note: half destroyed means half of the word is lost and only the other half survives

blocks.note: taken as written, the 's reading as is
the Isis is the Thames at Oxford, placed beside

explanation.surface: Farmers face disaster when floodwater ruins half the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of crop, CR, remains. The Isis is the name the Thames takes as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty that demands urgent action.

clue.text: He chases diamonds, possibly, as well as gold

blocks.note: diamonds is one suit in a pack of cards
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold-digger is after jewels and precious metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He chases' is a man pursuing a woman, not a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man who courts a woman, pursuing her in the hope of marriage.

clue.text: Elegant newcomer broadcasting

blocks.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman newly entering society
a programme on air is being broadcast

explanation.surface: A stylish new presenter takes to the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, stylish and charming manner, especially in a man, so it means elegant.

clue.text: Gorse covers it inside

indicators.note: whatever covers something goes all round it, so the shrub's letters enclose the pronoun

blocks.note: whin is another name for gorse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thick gorse bush hides something inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Whin is a northern English and Scottish word for gorse, the spiny yellow-flowered shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Within and inside are synonyms, both meaning in the interior of something.

clue.text: Current’s badly plugged into vehicle — bug develops

indicators.note: something plugged into a socket sits inside it, so these letters go within the vehicle

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
AC is alternating current
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A badly wired vehicle develops an electrical fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like a glitch in the wiring; here it is a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacillus is a rod-shaped bacterium, and bug is the informal word for a germ that causes illness.

clue.text: It’s again returned after city delivery

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the short prefix for again is read backwards

blocks.note: York is a cathedral city in northern England
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: A parcel is sent back yet again after being delivered to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests the post; in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a cricket ball bowled to pitch right at the batsman's feet, a type of delivery.

clue.text: Point in strait’s will find directions

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the possessive name of the strait

blocks.note: the Bering Strait separates Russia from Alaska, with the possessive S
A is taken as a single point, the top mark on a scale

explanation.surface: A navigator finds his way through a narrow strait.
explanation.walkthrough: Point for A is loose; the strait is the Bering Strait between Siberia and Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearings are compass directions taken to fix a position, as in getting one's bearings.
